extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer-algebra system (mathematicians / computational algebraists) needing reference for presolve.lib and solve.lib procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures (presolve.lib and solve.lib): usage, parameters, return values, notes, examples and warnings for elimination, variable analysis, and solving polynomial systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimpart
rubrics_metrics.description: elimpart(i [,n,e] ); i=ideal, n,e=integers. n: only the first n vars are considered for substitution, e=0: substitute from linear part of i (same as elimlinearpart), e!=0: eliminate also by direct substitution (default: n = nvars(basering), e = 1). Return: list of 5 objects describing substituted ideal, substituted variables, substitution formulas, variables set to 0 and a map describing the induced map of basering to itself (see doc for exact contents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed return entries: [1] ideal obtained by substituting from first n variables those appearing in linear part of i (or expressible if e!=0); [2] ideal of variables which have been substituted; [3] ideal where i-th element defines substitution of i-th var in [2]; [4] ideal of basering variables, substituted ones set to 0; [5] ideal describing the map from the basering to itself onto remaining variables and [1] is the image of i. The ideal i is generated by [1] and [3] and induces an isomorphism k[x(1..m)]/i -> k[..variables from [4]..]/[1]. Note: applying elimpart to interred(i) may result in more substitutions; interred may be more expansive than elimpart for big ideals. Examples provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: elimpartanyr
rubrics_metrics.description: elimpartanyr(i [,p,e] ); i=ideal, p=polynomial (product of vars to be eliminated), e=integer. e=0: substitute from linear part of i, e!=0: eliminate also by direct substitution. (default: p=product of all vars, e=1). Return: list of 6 objects: [1] interreduced ideal after substitutions, [2] ideal of substituted variables, [3] substitution formulas, [4] ideal of basering variables with substituted ones set to 0, [5] ideal describing the map and image, [6] int, number of vars considered (# factors of p).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ideal i is generated by [1] and [3] and induces an isomorphism k[x(1..m)]/i -> k[..variables from [4]..]/[1]. Note: procedure uses execute to create a ring with ordering dp and variables placed correctly and then applies elimpart. Example provided showing usage with single variable p.

rubrics_metrics.name: fastelim
rubrics_metrics.description: fastelim(i,p[h,o,a,b,e,m]); i=ideal, p=polynomial; optional integer flags h,o,a,b,e,m control heuristics. p: product of variables to be eliminated. Return: ideal obtained from i by eliminating those variables occurring in p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options (defaults: h,o,a,b,e,m = 0,1,0,0,0,0): h !=0 use Hilbert-series driven std-basis computation; o !=0 use proc valvars for (hopefully) optimal ordering; a !=0 order vars to be eliminated w.r.t increasing complexity; b !=0 order vars not eliminated w.r.t increasing complexity; e !=0 use elimpart first to eliminate easy part; m !=0 compute a minimal system of generators. Examples show typical calls and results. Useful as higher-level elimination combining heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: findvars
rubrics_metrics.description: findvars(id ); id = poly/ideal/vector/module/matrix. Return: list L with 4 entries: L[1] ideal of variables occurring in id, L[2] intvec of variables occurring in id, L[3] ideal of variables not occurring in id, L[4] intvec of variables not occurring in id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to inspect which basering variables actually occur in an object. Example shows returned lists and intvecs. See also reference to variables procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: hilbvec
rubrics_metrics.description: hilbvec(id[,c,o]); id=poly/ideal/vector/module/matrix, c,o=strings. Return: intvec of 1st Hilbert-series of id, computed in char c and ordering o (default c="32003", o="dp").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: id must be homogeneous (all variables have weight 1). Example shows calling after homogenization of ideal with an extra variable H. Returns coefficients of first Hilbert series as intvec. Provide char and ordering overrides if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: linearpart
rubrics_metrics.description: linearpart(id); id=ideal/module. Return: list of size 2: [1] generators of id of total degree <= 1, [2] remaining generators of id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: all variables have degree 1 (independent of basering ordering). Accepts modules (example provided using show(linearpart(m))). Useful to separate linear part from higher-degree generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: tolessvars
rubrics_metrics.description: tolessvars(id [,s1,s2] ); id poly/ideal/vector/module/matrix, s1=string (new ordering). If id contains all vars of the basering: empty list. Else: creates ring R with same char but possibly fewer variables (only those that occur in id); in R an object IMAG (image of id under imap) is stored. Default s1 chosen depending on first block of old ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If printlevel >=0 displays the variables omitted. Example shows creation of R_r, setting ring and accessing IMAG. After use, kill R_r recommended. Useful to create a ring with only the variables actually used.

rubrics_metrics.name: solvelinearpart
rubrics_metrics.description: solvelinearpart(id [,n] ); id=ideal/module, n=integer (default n=0). Return: (interreduced) generators of id of degree <=1 in reduced triangular form if n=0 [non-reduced triangular form if n!=0]. Assume monomial ordering is a global (p-)ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be used to solve systems of linear equations; alternative is gauss_row from matrix.lib. Warning: result likely false for 'real' coefficients — use char 0 instead. Example demonstrates solving a small linear system; with n=0 returns reduced triangular form (clear solution), n!=0 returns non-reduced triangular form.

rubrics_metrics.name: sortandmap
rubrics_metrics.description: sortandmap(id [,n1,p1,n2,p2...,o1,m1,o2,m2...]); id=poly/ideal/vector/module. pi are polynomials (products of variables), ni ints, oi strings, mi ints. Return: a ring R (different only in monomial ordering and variable sorting) in which IMAG (image of id under imap) is stored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New ordering/sorting: each block of vars occurring in pi is sorted w.r.t. its complexity in id; ni controls whether least (ni=0) or most (ni!=0) complex vars come first; oi and mi define ordering of i-th block (mi=0: oi is ordstr of block; mi!=0: blockordering). Only simple ordstrings allowed: "lp","dp","Dp","ls","ds","Ds". Complexity defined via val(x) (valuation vector) as lexicographic vector of maximal power and counts of monomials in coefficients. Examples show creating ring R_r and accessing IMAG. Useful to reorder variables/ordering optimally with respect to id for computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: sortvars
rubrics_metrics.description: sortvars(id[,n1,p1,n2,p2,...]); id=poly/ideal/vector/module, pi polynomials (product of vars), ni integers (defaults). Compute: sort variables with respect to their complexity in id. Return: list of two elements: [1] ideal, variables of basering sorted w.r.t. complexity; [2] list with 4 entries for each pi: (ai ideal of vars in correct order, vi intvec permutation, Mi valuation matrix, wi intvec sizes of blocks of identical valuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ni controls ordering in i-th block: ni=0 less complex first, ni!=0 more complex first. Includes examples and printed valuation matrices. Use to obtain variable ordering information; combine with sortandmap to create ring with new ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: valvars
rubrics_metrics.description: valvars(id[,n1,p1,n2,p2,...]); id=poly/ideal/vector/module, pi polynomials (product of vars), ni integers (defaults). Compute valuation/complexity of variables w.r.t id. Return: list with 3 entries: [1] intvec v describing permutation ordering variables by complexity, [2] list of intvecs v(i) describing permutations of vars in each factor, [3] list of ideals and intmat's a(i) and M(i) where a(i) factors of pi and M(i) valuation matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ni controls whether less (ni=0) or more (ni!=0) complex vars come first. Note: use sortvars to actually sort variables. Examples illustrate returned permutations and valuation matrices; intended to quantify variable complexity (val(x) as maximal occuring power etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: idealSplit
rubrics_metrics.description: idealSplit(id,timeF,timeS); id ideal and optional timeF, timeS integers to bound time for factorization respectively standard basis computation. Return: a list of ideals such that their intersection has the same radical as id.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to decompose ideal into components (intersection with same radical). Examples show various output ideals; parameters can be used to limit time spent on factorization and std-basis steps. Useful for splitting an ideal into more manageable components for further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: laguerre_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: laguerre_solve(f [, m, l, n, s] ); f = univariate polynomial; m,l,n,s integers controlling precision/behavior. Defaults (m,l,n,s) = (8,30,1,0). Return: list of (complex) roots of f; entries are strings if basering not complex, numbers otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parameter meanings: m = precision of output digits (>=4) if basering not complex; l = internal computation precision (>=8) if basering not complex; n controls multiplicity/splitting: n<0 no split, n>=0 try to split, n=0 return only distinct roots, n>0 find all roots with multiplicity; s !=0 returns ERROR if |f(root)| > 0.1^m. Basering must have char 0 and be complex or without parameters. If printlevel>0 displays comments. If s!=0 and ERROR occurs, try higher m. Examples show complex roots output and checking via subst.

rubrics_metrics.name: solve
rubrics_metrics.description: solve(G [, m, n [, l]] [,"oldring"] [,"nodisplay"] ); G = ideal, m,n,l = integers controlling precision and multiplicity (defaults (m,n,l)=(8,0,30) or (m,n,l)=(m,n,60) when n!=0 and only m,n set).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes ideal is zero-dimensional and basering char 0 and complex or without parameters. If called without "oldring": creates ring R with complex coefficients (precision m) and stores list SOL of complex solutions: if n=0 SOL lists all different solutions (each solution is a list of numbers); if n!=0, SOL is [distinct_solutions, multiplicities], ordered by multiplicity. If called with "oldring": interactively looks for appropriate top-level ring to store solutions and returns a string indicating export. If ideal not 0-dim, procedure errors. If G is not lex Groebner basis, lex Groebner basis computed internally (Hilbert driven). By default displays computed solutions unless "nodisplay" provided. Examples illustrate creating ring and accessing SOL and multiplicities.

rubrics_metrics.name: ures_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: ures_solve(i [, k, p] ); i = ideal (zero-dimensional quadratic system), k,p = integers. Defaults k=0, p=30. k=0 use sparse resultant matrix of Gelfand-Kapranov-Zelevinsky; k=1 use Macaulay resultant matrix (works only for homogeneous ideals); p controls precision of long floats for internal computation if basering not complex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes nvars(basering) = ncols(i) = number of vars actually occurring in i (quadratic system). If ground field is complex returns list of numbers (complex roots). Otherwise creates ring R with complex coefs and precision p and stores list SOL with complex roots. Example demonstrates computing intersection points of two curves and accessing SOL. Useful specialized solver for quadratic systems via resultant matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: mp_res_mat
rubrics_metrics.description: mp_res_mat(i [, k] ); i ideal, k integer (k=0 sparse resultant matrix of GKZ, k=1 Macaulay resultant matrix; default k=0). Number of elements in input system must be number of variables in basering plus one; if k=1 then i must be homogeneous. Return: module representing the multipolynomial resultant matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show construction of sparse and Macaulay resultant matrices, printing the module and computing determinant to get resultant polynomial. Also shows numerical example and determinant computation. Useful to form resultant matrices for elimination and resultant computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: interpolate
rubrics_metrics.description: interpolate(p,v,d); p,v = ideals of numbers, d=integer. Assume ground field K = Q, p and v are lists with size(p)=n (# vars) and size(v)=N=(d+1)^n, and p[j] != -1,0,1. Return: poly f, the unique polynomial of degree <= n*d with prescribed values v[i] at points p(i)=(p[1]^(i-1),..,p[n]^(i-1)), i=1..N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mainly useful when n=1 (univariate interpolation). Example shows reconstructing polynomial from values at powers of 3. See also Vandermonde reference. Ensures unique interpolant under stated assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: fglm_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: fglm_solve(i [, p] ); i ideal, p integer (precision). Assume ground field char 0. Return: ring R with complex coefficients (precision p) containing rlist, a list of complex roots of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure uses a standard basis of i to determine complex roots. p>0 gives precision (default p=30). Examples show calling to compute intersection points of curves and accessing rlist. Useful when standard-basis-based root extraction via FGLM is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: lex_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: lex_solve(i[,p] ); i = reduced lexicographical Groebner basis of a zero-dimensional ideal, sorted by increasing leading terms. p>0 gives precision of complex numbers (default p=30). Return: ring R with complex coefficients and a list rlist of complex roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes input is a reduced lex Groebner basis. The procedure converts lexicographic triangular form into numerical roots (ring with complex precision). Example shows computing intersection points after stdfglm and passing to lex_solve. Use when lex Groebner basis is already available to extract roots efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: simplexOut
rubrics_metrics.description: simplexOut(l); l = list (output of simplex). Return: Nothing (procedure prints the computed solution of simplex as strings in a nice format).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes l is output from simplex. Example shows formatting maximization result with constraints and the printed solution (objective z and variable values). Useful for displaying linear programming results from simplex in a human-readable format.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangLf_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: triangLf_solve(i [, p] ); i ideal, p integer (precision). Assumes ground field char 0 and i zero-dimensional. Return: ring R with complex coefficients (precision p) containing rlist of complex roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure uses a triangular system computed by Lazard’s algorithm with factorization (from a standard basis) and recursively determines all complex roots using Laguerre’s algorithm. p>0 sets numeric precision (default p=30). Example shows usage for intersection of curves. Useful when triangularization via Lazard+factorization is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: triangM_solve
rubrics_metrics.description: triangM_solve(i [, p ] ); i ideal, p integer (precision). Assumes ground field char 0 and i zero-dimensional. Return: ring R with complex coefficients (precision p) containing rlist of complex roots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure uses a triangular system computed by Moeller’s algorithm (from a standard basis) and recursively determines all complex roots using Laguerre’s algorithm. p>0 sets numeric precision (default p=30). Example shows usage for intersection of curves. Useful alternative triangularization method (Moeller) for solving zero-dimensional systems.
